    23                  Proclamation 11047 of July 20, 2026
    24  
    25                  
    26  Imposing Additional Duties To Offset Canadian 
    27                  Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United 
    28                  States With Respect to Dairy
    29  
    30                  By the President of the United States of America
    31  
    32                  A Proclamation
    33  
    34                  1. Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 
    35                  1338) (section 338) empowers the President to, among 
    36                  other things, impose duties on imports of a foreign 
    37                  country to offset the burden or disadvantage from a 
    38                  foreign country's discrimination against or unequal 
    39                  imposition on the commerce of the United States.
    40  
    41                  2. Canada, through discrimination or an unreasonable 
    42                  and unequal imposition, treats the commerce of certain 
    43                  foreign countries more favorably than commerce of the 
    44                  United States with respect to dairy and in turn, places 
    45                  a burden and disadvantage on the commerce of the United 
    46                  States. Specifically, Canada denies the commerce of the 
    47                  United States benefits that Canada affords to 
    48                  materially similar dairy commerce from certain other 
    49                  foreign countries and thus unreasonably burdens and 
    50                  disadvantages U.S. commerce compared to the commerce of 
    51                  certain other foreign countries.
    52  
    53                  3. Canada maintains a tariff-rate quota (TRQ) on 
    54                  cheeses of all types under the United States-Mexico-
    55                  Canada Agreement (USMCA) as well as a TRQ on cheese of 
    56                  all types under the Canada-European Union (EU) 
    57                  Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). The 
    58                  TRQs provide duty-free access for the covered dairy 
    59                  products up to specified annual quantities (in-quota 
    60                  quantities) and apply a customs duty to imports that 
    61                  exceed the respective in-quota quantities.
    62  
    63                  4. To access the TRQs under the USMCA and the CETA, 
    64                  Canada's dairy TRQ allocation measures establish 
    65                  eligibility criteria. But Canada does not have the same 
    66                  eligibility criteria for the USMCA and the CETA, 
    67                  disfavoring the commerce of the United States. While 
    68                  Canada's eligibility criteria for the USMCA dairy 
    69                  TRQs--and specifically, the cheeses of all types TRQ--
    70                  do not allow retailers to obtain and use TRQ 
    71                  quantities, the eligibility criteria for the CETA do 
    72                  grant retailers access to the TRQ quantity for cheese 
    73                  of all types.
    74  
    75                  5. By making retailers ineligible to use the USMCA TRQ 
    76                  for cheeses of all types, Canada discriminates against 
    77                  U.S. goods that are similar to EU goods that are 
    78                  entered pursuant to the CETA cheese of all types TRQ. 
    79                  Canada thus denies to the United States the favorable 
    80                  treatment that Canada provides to the EU and its member 
    81                  States. This discrimination impedes market access into 
    82                  Canada and results in lost sales or revenues for U.S. 
    83                  dairy producers and exporters, among other things. The 
    84                  United States, U.S. businesses and workers, and U.S. 
    85                  commerce are negatively affected by Canada's 
    86                  discriminatory practices.
    87  
    88                  6. Accordingly, pursuant to section 338, I find as a 
    89                  fact that Canada is discriminating in fact against the 
    90                  commerce of the United States through Canada's TRQ 
    91                  allocation measures imposed on U.S. cheeses of all 
    92                  types under the USMCA, as compared to Canada's TRQ 
    93                  allocation measures imposed on EU cheese of all types 
    94                  under the CETA. I also find as a fact that this 
    95                  discrimination places the commerce of the United States 
    96                  at a
    97  
    98  [[Page 46654]]
    99  
   100                  disadvantage compared to the commerce of the EU and its 
   101                  member States. And I find as fact that Canada's 
   102                  imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced 
   103                  upon the like articles of every foreign country, and 
   104                  places a burden on the commerce of the United States.
   105  
   106                  7. Further, I find that imposing additional ad valorem 
   107                  duties on certain products of Canada to address the 
   108                  burden or disadvantage from this discrimination or 
   109                  unequal and unreasonable imposition is in the public 
   110                  interest, will serve the public interest, and is 
   111                  consistent with the interests of the United States. 
   112                  When U.S. producers are unfairly denied export 
   113                  opportunities by Canada's TRQ allocation measures, they 
   114                  lose sales or revenues that support production in the 
   115                  United States, among other things. This suppresses U.S. 
   116                  agricultural output as well as investment and thereby 
   117                  undermines employment and economic vitality in American 
   118                  communities. Imposing additional duties on certain 
   119                  products of Canada will, among other things, expand 
   120                  opportunities for U.S. producers to compete within the 
   121                  U.S. market, enhancing American production and bringing 
   122                  attendant economic and societal benefits, and may spur 
   123                  Canada to remove the discrimination against U.S. 
   124                  cheeses of all types.
   125  
   126                  8. Accordingly, I find that it is necessary and 
   127                  appropriate and in the public interest to impose an 
   128                  additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent on certain 
   129                  products of Canada, as identified in Annex II to this 
   130                  proclamation, effective as of 12:01 a.m. eastern time 
   131                  on August 19, 2026. I determine that the additional ad 
   132                  valorem duties imposed in this proclamation, as 
   133                  described below, will offset the burden or disadvantage 
   134                  on U.S. commerce from Canada's discrimination or 
   135                  unreasonable and unequal imposition. In my judgment, 
   136                  the action in this proclamation is consistent with the 
   137                  public interest, will serve the public interest, and is 
   138                  consistent with the interests of the United States.
   139  
   140                  9. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   141                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   142                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   143                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   144                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   145                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   146                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   147                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   148                  finding that a foreign country imposes an unreasonable 
   149                  charge, exaction, regulation, or limitation that is not 
   150                  equally enforced on the like articles of every foreign 
   151                  country, or discriminates in fact against U.S. commerce 
   152                  in a way that places the commerce of the United States 
   153                  at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of any 
   154                  foreign country. Section 338 also authorizes the 
   155                  President to suspend, revoke, supplement, or amend any 
   156                  proclamation under section 338 whenever the President 
   157                  deems that the public interests require such action. 
   158                  Further, section 338 authorizes the President to 
   159                  exclude products of the foreign country if the foreign 
   160                  country maintains or increases the discrimination 
   161                  against the commerce of the United States and the 
   162                  President deems the exclusion to be consistent with the 
   163                  public interests and the interests of the United 
   164                  States.
   165  
   166                  10. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended 
   167                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the 
   168                  President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule 
   169                  of the United States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes 
   170                  affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, 
   171                  including the removal, modification, continuance, or 
   172                  imposition of any rate of duty or other import 
   173                  restriction.
   174  
   175                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   176                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   177                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   178                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   179                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   180                  follows:
   181  
   182  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation, certain products of 
   183  Canada, as set forth in Annex II to this proclamation, imported into the 
   184  United States shall be subject to an additional ad valorem duty of 50 
   185  percent, effective for goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   186  warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
   187  19, 2026.
   188  
   189  [[Page 46655]]
   190  
   191  (2) Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation and in Annex I to 
   192  this proclamation, the duties imposed in this proclamation are in addition 
   193  to any other duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges applicable to such 
   194  products. The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to 
   195  articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232 of the Trade Expansion 
   196  Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1862), or articles, excluding unmanned 
   197  aircraft, subject to the World Trade Organization Agreement on Trade in 
   198  Civil Aircraft.
   199  
   200  (3) The HTSUS is modified as provided in Annex II to this proclamation, 
   201  effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   202  warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
   203  19, 2026, and the modifications shall continue in effect, unless this 
   204  action is expressly reduced, modified, or terminated.
   205  
   206  (4) Any product subject to the duties imposed in this proclamation, except 
   207  those eligible for admission under ``domestic status'' as described in 19 
   208  CFR 146.43, that is subject to the duties imposed in this proclamation and 
   209  that is admitted into a United States foreign trade zone on or after the 
   210  effective date of this proclamation must be admitted as ``privileged 
   211  foreign status'' as described in 19 CFR 146.41, and will be subject upon 
   212  entry for consumption to any ad valorem rate of duty related to the 
   213  classification under the applicable HTSUS subheading.
   214  
   215  (5) The head of each executive department and agency (agency) is authorized 
   216  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   217  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency may, consistent with 
   218  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
   219  redelegate the authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   220  agency.
   221  
   222  (6) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in 
   223  consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, 
   224  and the United States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue such 
   225  rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or determinations as may be 
   226  necessary to implement this proclamation and is authorized to take any 
   227  necessary measures to administer the duties imposed in this proclamation.
   228  
   229  (7) The Commissioner of CBP, in consultation with the Secretary of the 
   230  Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, the United States Trade 
   231  Representative, the Chairman of the United States International Trade 
   232  Commission, and any other senior official he deems appropriate, shall 
   233  determine whether any additional modifications to the HTSUS are necessary 
   234  to effectuate this proclamation and shall make such modifications to the 
   235  HTSUS through notice in the Federal Register, including any technical 
   236  correction to the annexes to this proclamation.
   237  
   238  (8) For any rule or regulation the Commissioner of CBP makes to implement 
   239  this proclamation, the Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by 
   240  law, obtain the approval of the President or the United States Trade 
   241  Representative. The United States Trade Representative is delegated the 
   242  President's approval authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).
   243  
   244  (9) Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that is 
   245  inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such 
   246  inconsistency. If any provision of this proclamation or the application of 
   247  any provision to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the 
   248  remainder of this proclamation and the application of its provisions to any 
   249  other individuals or circumstances shall not be affected.
   250  
   251  [[Page 46656]]
   252  
   253                  IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this 
   254                  twentieth day of July, in the year of our Lord two 
   255                  thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the 
   256                  United States of America the two hundred and fifty-
   257                  first.

    24  
    25                  
    26  Imposing Additional Duties To Offset Canadian 
    27                  Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United 
    28                  States With Respect to Motor Vehicles
    29  
    30                  By the President of the United States of America
    31  
    32                  A Proclamation
    33  
    34                  1. Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 
    35                  1338) (section 338) empowers the President to, among 
    36                  other things, impose duties on imports of a foreign 
    37                  country to offset the burden or disadvantage from a 
    38                  foreign country's discrimination against or unequal 
    39                  imposition on the commerce of the United States.
    40  
    41                  2. Canada, through discrimination against or an 
    42                  unreasonable and unequal imposition on U.S. auto and 
    43                  auto parts exports, burdens U.S. commerce but not the 
    44                  commerce of other countries and disadvantages U.S. 
    45                  commerce compared to the commerce of other countries. 
    46                  Specifically, Canada imposed a tariff system on only 
    47                  U.S. motor vehicles and treats the commerce of foreign 
    48                  countries more favorably than commerce of the United 
    49                  States with respect to motor vehicles, as defined in 
    50                  Canada's United States Surtax Order (Motor Vehicles 
    51                  2025), SOR/2025-118. By denying to the commerce of the 
    52                  United States the benefits afforded to like commerce 
    53                  from other countries, Canada discriminates against U.S. 
    54                  commerce, disadvantaging the commerce of the United 
    55                  States compared to the commerce of other countries. And 
    56                  Canada's imposition on U.S. motor vehicles is 
    57                  unreasonable, is not equally applied upon the like 
    58                  articles of every foreign country, and places a burden 
    59                  on the commerce of the United States but not on the 
    60                  commerce of other countries.
    61  
    62                  3. Since April 9, 2025, Canada has maintained a 25 
    63                  percent tariff rate on imports of U.S. motor vehicles 
    64                  that do not qualify for preferential, duty-free 
    65                  treatment under the United States-Mexico-Canada 
    66                  Agreement (USMCA). For U.S. motor vehicles that do 
    67                  qualify for preferential, duty-free treatment under the 
    68                  USMCA, Canada applies a 25 percent tariff rate on the 
    69                  value of all goods that do not originate in Canada or 
    70                  Mexico used in the production of the vehicle, up to 85 
    71                  percent of the total value of the vehicle. In addition, 
    72                  Canada maintains a tariff-rate quota (TRQ) on U.S. 
    73                  motor vehicles that qualify for preferential, duty-free 
    74                  treatment under the USMCA. The TRQ for each automaker 
    75                  limits duty-free access for the covered motor vehicles 
    76                  from that automaker up to certain annual quantities 
    77                  (in-quota quantities) and applies the tariffs described 
    78                  above on products that exceed the in-quota quantities. 
    79                  The TRQs are granted to induce companies to invest in 
    80                  production in Canada, and Canada has announced that it 
    81                  reduced the TRQs for U.S. companies that moved 
    82                  manufacturing from Canada to the United States. Canada 
    83                  does not publicly disclose the company-specific, in-
    84                  quota quantities, but it has published these new tariff 
    85                  rates in Customs Notice 25-15: United States Surtax 
    86                  Order (Motor Vehicles 2025).
    87  
    88                  4. The United States, U.S. businesses and workers, and 
    89                  U.S. commerce suffer from Canada's discriminatory, 
    90                  unequal, and unreasonable tariff scheme. Following the 
    91                  implementation of the tariff scheme, U.S. exports of 
    92                  motor vehicles to Canada fell precipitously. Comparing 
    93                  the period from April 2025 through March 2026 to the 
    94                  same period in 2024-2025, imports of U.S.
    95  
    96  [[Page 46664]]
    97  
    98                  motor vehicles to Canada decreased by approximately 22 
    99                  percent (from approximately $25.9 billion to 
   100                  approximately $20.3 billion).
   101  
   102                  5. Canada only applies the tariff scheme to U.S.-origin 
   103                  motor vehicles. The tariff scheme does not apply to the 
   104                  motor vehicles of any other country. Indeed, exports of 
   105                  motor vehicles from other countries to Canada have 
   106                  increased to meet the demand previously filled by U.S. 
   107                  exports. For example, comparing the period from April 
   108                  2025 through February 2026 to the same period in 2024-
   109                  2025, Canadian imports of Mexican motor vehicles 
   110                  increased by approximately 23.6 percent, and imports 
   111                  from Japan, Korea, and Germany increased by rates 
   112                  ranging from approximately 10.1 percent to 
   113                  approximately 13.5 percent. In total, Canadian imports 
   114                  of motor vehicles from countries other than the United 
   115                  States increased by approximately $2.85 billion over 
   116                  the same period, with Mexico accounting for almost $2 
   117                  billion of the increase.
   118  
   119                  6. Accordingly, pursuant to section 338, I find as a 
   120                  fact that Canada is discriminating against the commerce 
   121                  of the United States through Canada's motor vehicle 
   122                  tariff scheme. I also find as a fact that this 
   123                  discrimination places the commerce of the United States 
   124                  at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of other 
   125                  countries. And I find as fact that Canada's imposition 
   126                  is unreasonable, is not equally enforced upon the like 
   127                  articles of every foreign country, and places a burden 
   128                  on the commerce of the United States.
   129  
   130                  7. Further, I find that imposing additional ad valorem 
   131                  duties on certain products of Canada to address the 
   132                  burden or disadvantage from this discrimination or 
   133                  unequal and unreasonable imposition is in the public 
   134                  interest, will serve the public interest, and is 
   135                  consistent with the interests of the United States. 
   136                  When U.S. producers are unfairly denied export 
   137                  opportunities by Canada's motor vehicle tariffs and 
   138                  TRQs, they lose revenues that support production in the 
   139                  United States, among other things. This suppresses U.S. 
   140                  industrial output, as well as investment, and thereby 
   141                  undermines employment and economic vitality in American 
   142                  communities. Imposing additional duties on certain 
   143                  products of Canada will, among other things, expand 
   144                  opportunities for U.S. producers to compete within the 
   145                  U.S. market, enhancing American production and bringing 
   146                  attendant economic and societal benefits, and may spur 
   147                  Canada to remove the discrimination against U.S. motor 
   148                  vehicles.
   149  
   150                  8. Accordingly, I find that it is necessary and 
   151                  appropriate and in the public interest to impose an 
   152                  additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent on certain 
   153                  products of Canada, as identified in Annex II to this 
   154                  proclamation, effective as of 12:01 a.m. eastern time 
   155                  on August 19, 2026. I determine that the additional ad 
   156                  valorem duties imposed in this proclamation, as 
   157                  described below, will offset the burden or disadvantage 
   158                  on U.S. commerce from Canada's discrimination or 
   159                  unequal and unreasonable imposition. In my judgment, 
   160                  the action in this proclamation is consistent with the 
   161                  public interest, will serve the public interest, and is 
   162                  consistent with the interests of the United States.
   163  
   164                  9. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   165                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   166                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   167                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   168                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   169                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   170                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   171                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   172                  finding that a foreign country imposes an unreasonable 
   173                  charge, exaction, regulation, or limitation that is not 
   174                  equally enforced on the like articles of every foreign 
   175                  country, or discriminates in fact against U.S. commerce 
   176                  in a way that places the commerce of the United States 
   177                  at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of any 
   178                  foreign country. Section 338 also authorizes the 
   179                  President to suspend, revoke, supplement, or amend any 
   180                  proclamation under section 338 whenever the President 
   181                  deems that the public interests require such action. 
   182                  Further, section 338 authorizes the President to 
   183                  exclude articles of the foreign country if the foreign 
   184                  country maintains or increases the discrimination 
   185                  against the
   186  
   187  [[Page 46665]]
   188  
   189                  commerce of the United States and the President deems 
   190                  the exclusion to be consistent with the public 
   191                  interests and the interests of the United States.
   192  
   193                  10. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended 
   194                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the 
   195                  President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule 
   196                  of the United States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes 
   197                  affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, 
   198                  including the removal, modification, continuance, or 
   199                  imposition of any rate of duty or other import 
   200                  restriction.
   201  
   202                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   203                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   204                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   205                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   206                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   207                  follows:
   208  
   209  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation, certain products of 
   210  Canada, as set forth in Annex II to this proclamation, imported into the 
   211  United States shall be subject to an additional ad valorem duty of 50 
   212  percent, effective for goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   213  warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
   214  19, 2026.
   215  
   216  (2) Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation and in Annex I to 
   217  this proclamation, the duties imposed in this proclamation are in addition 
   218  to any other duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges applicable to such 
   219  products. The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to 
   220  articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232 of the Trade Expansion 
   221  Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1862), or articles, excluding unmanned 
   222  aircraft, subject to the World Trade Organization Agreement on Trade in 
   223  Civil Aircraft.
   224  
   225  (3) The HTSUS is modified as provided in Annex II to this proclamation, 
   226  effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   227  warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
   228  19, 2026, and the modifications shall continue in effect, unless this 
   229  action is expressly reduced, modified, or terminated.
   230  
   231  (4) Any product subject to the duties imposed in this proclamation, except 
   232  those eligible for admission under ``domestic status'' as described in 19 
   233  CFR 146.43, that is subject to the duties imposed in this proclamation and 
   234  that is admitted into a United States foreign trade zone on or after the 
   235  effective date of this proclamation must be admitted as ``privileged 
   236  foreign status'' as described in 19 CFR 146.41, and will be subject upon 
   237  entry for consumption to any ad valorem rate of duty related to the 
   238  classification under the applicable HTSUS subheading.
   239  
   240  (5) The head of each executive department and agency (agency) is authorized 
   241  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   242  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency may, consistent with 
   243  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
   244  redelegate the authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   245  agency.
   246  
   247  (6) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in 
   248  consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, 
   249  and the United States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue such 
   250  rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or determinations as may be 
   251  necessary to implement this proclamation and is authorized to take any 
   252  necessary measures to administer the duties imposed in this proclamation.

   254  (7) The Commissioner of CBP, in consultation with the Secretary of the 
   255  Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, the United States Trade 
   256  Representative, the Chairman of the United States International Trade 
   257  Commission, and any other senior official he deems appropriate, shall 
   258  determine whether any additional modifications to the HTSUS are necessary 
   259  to effectuate this proclamation and shall make such modifications to the 
   260  HTSUS through notice in the Federal Register, including any technical 
   261  correction to the annexes to this proclamation.
   262  
   263  [[Page 46666]]
   264  
   265  (8) For any rule or regulation the Commissioner of CBP makes to implement 
   266  this proclamation, the Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by

   268  Representative. The United States Trade Representative is delegated the 
   269  President's approval authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).
   270  
   271  (9) Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that is 
   272  inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such

    59                  
    60  Temporary Suspension of Additional Duties To 
    61                  Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of 
    62                  the United States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages, 
    63                  Dairy, and Motor Vehicles
    64  
    65                  By the President of the United States of America
    66  
    67                  A Proclamation
    68  
    69                  1. In Proclamation 11046 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing 
    70                  Additional Duties to Offset Canadian Discrimination 
    71                  Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect 
    72                  to Alcoholic Beverages), I found as a fact that Canada 
    73                  is discriminating against the commerce of the United 
    74                  States by banning the purchase, distribution, or 
    75                  retailing of U.S. alcoholic beverages while not banning 
    76                  or similarly restricting such products from other 
    77                  countries; that this discrimination places the commerce 
    78                  of the United States at a disadvantage compared to the 
    79                  commerce of other countries; and that Canada's 
    80                  imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced 
    81                  upon the like articles of every foreign country, and 
    82                  places a burden on the commerce of the United States. 
    83                  To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce 
    84                  from Canada's discrimination or unreasonable and 
    85                  unequal imposition on U.S. alcoholic beverages, I 
    86                  imposed under section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 
    87                  U.S.C. 1338) (section 338) additional ad valorem 
    88                  duties, effective August 19, 2026, on certain imports 
    89                  of Canada.
    90  
    91                  2. In Proclamation 11047 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing 
    92                  Additional Duties to Offset Canadian Discrimination 
    93                  Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect 
    94                  to Dairy), I found as a fact that Canada is 
    95                  discriminating against the commerce of the United 
    96                  States through Canada's tariff-rate quota allocation 
    97                  measures imposed on U.S. cheeses of all types; that 
    98                  this discrimination places the commerce of the United 
    99                  States at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of 
   100                  other countries; and that Canada's imposition is 
   101                  unreasonable, is not equally enforced upon the like 
   102                  articles of every foreign country, and places a burden 
   103                  on the commerce of the United States. To offset the 
   104                  burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce from Canada's 
   105                  discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition 
   106                  on U.S. dairy, I imposed under section 338 additional 
   107                  ad valorem duties, effective August 19, 2026, on 
   108                  certain imports of Canada.
   109  
   110                  3. In Proclamation 11048 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing 
   111                  Additional Duties to Offset Canadian Discrimination 
   112                  Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect 
   113                  to Motor Vehicles), I found as a fact that Canada is 
   114                  discriminating against the commerce of the United 
   115                  States through Canada's motor vehicle tariff scheme; 
   116                  that this discrimination places the commerce of the 
   117                  United States at a disadvantage compared to the 
   118                  commerce of other countries; and that Canada's 
   119                  imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced 
   120                  upon the like articles of every foreign country, and 
   121                  places a burden on the commerce of the United States. 
   122                  To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce 
   123                  from Canada's discrimination or unreasonable and 
   124                  unequal imposition on U.S. auto and auto parts exports, 
   125                  I imposed under section 338 additional ad valorem 
   126                  duties, effective August 19, 2026, on certain imports 
   127                  of Canada.
   128  
   129                  4. I have received certain information, opinions, and 
   130                  recommendations from senior executive branch officials 
   131                  on the status of the circumstances involved
   132  
   133  [[Page 54790]]
   134  
   135                  in Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048 and of 
   136                  negotiations between the United States and Canada 
   137                  regarding the discriminations or impositions described 
   138                  in Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048. According to 
   139                  senior executive branch officials, Canada has expressed 
   140                  a commitment to remove the discriminations or 
   141                  unreasonable and unequal impositions at issue in 
   142                  Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048. In these 
   143                  officials' opinion, because of the status of these 
   144                  negotiations, the public interests favor suspending for 
   145                  a period of 3 days the additional duties imposed in 
   146                  Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048.
   147  
   148                  5. After considering the information, opinions, and 
   149                  recommendations that have been provided to me by senior 
   150                  executive branch officials, among other relevant 
   151                  information and considerations, I determine that in 
   152                  these circumstances, the public interest requires 
   153                  suspending for a period of 3 days the additional ad 
   154                  valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046, 11047, 
   155                  and 11048.
   156  
   157                  6. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   158                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   159                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   160                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   161                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   162                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   163                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   164                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   165                  finding that a foreign country imposes an unreasonable 
   166                  charge, exaction, regulation, or limitation that is not 
   167                  equally enforced on the like articles of every foreign 
   168                  country, or discriminates in fact against U.S. commerce 
   169                  in a way that places the commerce of the United States 
   170                  at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of any 
   171                  foreign country. Section 338 also authorizes the 
   172                  President to suspend, revoke, supplement, or amend any 
   173                  proclamation under section 338 whenever the President 
   174                  deems that the public interests require such action.
   175  
   176                  7. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 
   177                  U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the President to 
   178                  embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United 
   179                  States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes affecting 
   180                  import treatment, and actions thereunder, including the 
   181                  removal, modification, continuance, or imposition of 
   182                  any rate of duty or other import restriction.
   183  
   184                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   185                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   186                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   187                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   188                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   189                  follows:
   190  
   191  (1) The effective date of the additional ad valorem duties imposed in 
   192  Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048 shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   193  August 22, 2026. Accordingly, the chapeau of Annex II of each of 
   194  Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048, is amended by deleting the effective 
   195  date ``August 19, 2026'' and inserting ``August 22, 2026'' in lieu thereof.
   196  
   197  (2) The head of each executive department and agency (agency), to the 
   198  extent consistent with law, is authorized to and shall take all appropriate 
   199  steps to implement this proclamation. The head of each agency shall, to the 
   200  extent consistent with law, immediately begin taking steps to effectuate 
   201  this proclamation and, as soon as practicable, suspend the collection of 
   202  the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 
   203  11048 to the extent required to effectuate this proclamation. The head of 
   204  each agency may, consistent with applicable law, including section 301 of 
   205  title 3, United States Code, redelegate within the agency the authority to 
   206  take such appropriate steps.
   207  
   208  (3) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in 
   209  consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, 
   210  the United States Trade Representative, the Chairman of the United States 
   211  International Trade Commission, and any other senior executive branch 
   212  official he deems appropriate, shall determine whether any additional 
   213  modifications to the HTSUS are necessary to effectuate this proclamation
   214  
   215  [[Page 54791]]
   216  
   217  and shall make such modifications to the HTSUS through notice in the 
   218  Federal Register.
   219  
   220  (4) To the extent that implementation of this proclamation requires a 
   221  refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed pursuant to 
   222  applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds.
   223  
   224  (5) Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that is 
   225  inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such 
   226  inconsistency. If any provision of this proclamation or the application of 
   227  any provision to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the 
   228  remainder of this proclamation and the application of its provisions to any 
   229  other individuals or circumstances shall not be affected.
   230  
   231                  IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this 
   232                  eighteenth day of August, in the year of our Lord two 
   233                  thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the 
   234                  United States of America the two hundred and fifty-
   235                  first.

   160                  levy on U.S. alcoholic beverages, effective September

   165                  in response to the additional ad valorem duties imposed 
   166                  in Proclamation 11046. In my senior executive branch 
   167                  officials' opinion, an import ban on certain Canadian

   169                  ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046 is

   177                  that Canada has, after the issuance of Proclamation 
   178                  11046 and after the additional ad valorem duties 
   179                  imposed in Proclamation 11046 became effective,

   181                  commerce of the United States described in Proclamation 
   182                  11046.

   186                  directing that certain products of Canada that are 
   187                  currently subject to the additional ad valorem duties

   190                  is consistent with the public interests to exclude from 
   191                  importation into the United States certain alcoholic 
   192                  beverages of Canada that are currently subject to the

   194                  11046, as further detailed in the Annex to this 
   195                  proclamation.

   198                  consistent with the public interests and the interests

   200                  interests, and will serve the public interest.

   220                  public interests require such action. Further, section

   121                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   122                  of the United States, is required by the public 
   123                  interests, and will serve the public interest.

   126                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   127                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   128                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   129                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   130                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   131                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   132                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   133                  finding that a foreign country is imposing an 
   134                  unreasonable charge, exaction, regulation, or 
   135                  limitation that is not equally enforced on the like 
   136                  articles of every foreign country, or discriminates in 
   137                  fact against U.S. commerce in a way that places the 
   138                  commerce of the United States at a disadvantage 
   139                  compared to the commerce of any foreign country.

   141                  revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under 
   142                  section 338 whenever the President deems that the 
   143                  public interests require such action. Further, section 
   144                  338 authorizes the President to exclude from 
   145                  importation articles of the foreign country if the 
   146                  foreign country maintains or increases the 
   147                  discrimination against the commerce of the United 
   148                  States and the President deems the exclusion to be 
   149                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   150                  of the United States.

   153                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the

   162                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me

   165                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as

   175  warehouse for consumption, prior to September 29, 2026, will remain subject

   192  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to

   194  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code,

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

   132                  338 authorizes the President to exclude from 
   133                  importation articles of the foreign country if the 
   134                  foreign country maintains or increases the 
   135                  discrimination against the commerce of the United 
   136                  States and the President deems the exclusion to be 
   137                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   138                  of the United States.

   140                  9. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 
   141                  U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the President to 
   142                  embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United 
   143                  States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes affecting 
   144                  import treatment, and actions thereunder, including the 
   145                  removal, modification, continuance, or imposition of 
   146                  any rate of duty or other import restriction.

   148                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   149                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   150                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   151                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   152                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   153                  follows:

   155  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation, certain products of 
   156  Canada, as set forth in Annex I, Part A to this proclamation, imported into 
   157  the United States shall be subject to the additional ad valorem duty of 50 
   158  percent imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11048. In addition, certain 
   159  products of Canada, as set forth in Annex I, Part B to this proclamation, 
   160  imported into the United States shall no longer be subject to the 
   161  additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent imposed pursuant to Proclamation 
   162  11048. The duties imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as modified in 
   163  this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to 
   164  section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 
   165  1862). These changes shall be effective with respect to goods entered for 
   166  consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 
   167  a.m. eastern time on September 15, 2026.

   170  effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   171  warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on September 
   172  15, 2026, and the modifications shall continue in effect unless this action 
   173  is expressly suspended, revoked, supplemented, amended, or terminated.
   174  
   175  (3) The head of each executive department and agency (agency) is authorized 
   176  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   177  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency may, consistent with 
   178  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States

   185  (4) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in

    65  
    66                  By the President of the United States of America
    67  
    68                  A Proclamation
    69  
    70                  1. In Proclamation 11048 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing 
    71                  Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination 
    72                  Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect 
    73                  to Motor Vehicles), I found as a fact that Canada is 
    74                  discriminating in fact against the commerce of the 
    75                  United States through Canada's motor vehicle tariff 
    76                  scheme; that this discrimination places the commerce of 
    77                  the United States at a disadvantage compared to the 
    78                  commerce of other countries; and that Canada's 
    79                  imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced 
    80                  upon the like articles of every foreign country, and 
    81                  places a burden on the commerce of the United States. 
    82                  To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce 
    83                  from Canada's discrimination or unreasonable and 
    84                  unequal imposition on U.S. auto and auto parts exports, 
    85                  I imposed under section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 
    86                  (19 U.S.C. 1338) (section 338) additional ad valorem 
    87                  duties, effective August 19, 2026, on certain products 
    88                  of Canada.
    89  
    90                  2. In Proclamation 11056 of August 18, 2026 (Temporary 
    91                  Suspension of Additional Duties To Offset Canadian 
    92                  Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United 
    93                  States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages, Dairy, and 
    94                  Motor Vehicles), I temporarily suspended for 3 days the 
    95                  effective date of the additional ad valorem duties 
    96                  imposed under Proclamation 11048 after Canada expressed 
    97                  a commitment to remove the discrimination or 
    98                  unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in 
    99                  Proclamation 11048.
   100  
   101                  3. On August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its 
   102                  commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did 
   103                  not remove the discrimination or unreasonable and 
   104                  unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11048.
   105  
   106                  4. Accordingly, at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
   107                  22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 
   108                  11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties 
   109                  imposed under Proclamation 11048 became effective.
   110  
   111                  5. In Proclamation 11065 of September 8, 2026 
   112                  (Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada Subject to 
   113                  the Additional Duties Imposed To Offset Canadian 
   114                  Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United 
   115                  States With Respect to Motor Vehicles), I modified the 
   116                  duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 after receiving 
   117                  certain information, opinions, and recommendations from 
   118                  senior executive branch officials to continue 
   119                  offsetting the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce 
   120                  and better serve the public interest.
   121  
   122                  6. I have received certain additional information, 
   123                  opinions, and recommendations from senior executive 
   124                  branch officials on the status of the circumstances 
   125                  involved in Proclamation 11048 and the effect of the 
   126                  additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 
   127                  11048, as amended, including how effectively those 
   128                  duties are offsetting the burden or disadvantage on 
   129                  U.S. commerce. According to senior executive branch 
   130                  officials, although the additional ad valorem duties 
   131                  imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, offset the 
   132                  burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce, modifying the 
   133                  scope of products
   134  
   135  [[Page 68862]]
   136  
   137                  subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in 
   138                  Proclamation 11048, as amended, would still offset the 
   139                  burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce and better 
   140                  serve the public interest. In my senior executive 
   141                  branch officials' opinion, modifying the scope of 
   142                  products subject to the additional ad valorem duties 
   143                  imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, is required 
   144                  by the public interests and is consistent with the 
   145                  interests of the United States.
   146  
   147                  7. After considering the information, opinions, and 
   148                  recommendations that have been provided to me by senior 
   149                  executive branch officials, among other relevant 
   150                  information and considerations, I determine that the 
   151                  public interests require modifying the scope of 
   152                  products subject to the additional ad valorem duties 
   153                  imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended.
   154  
   155                  8. In my judgment, the modification in this 
   156                  proclamation will offset the burden or disadvantage on 
   157                  U.S. commerce, is consistent with the public interests 
   158                  and the interests of the United States, is required by 
   159                  the public interests, and will better serve the public 
   160                  interest.
   161  
   162                  9. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   163                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   164                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   165                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   166                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   167                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   168                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   169                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   170                  finding that a foreign country is imposing an 
   171                  unreasonable charge, exaction, regulation, or 
   172                  limitation that is not equally enforced on the like 
   173                  articles of every foreign country, or discriminates in 
   174                  fact against U.S. commerce in a way that places the 
   175                  commerce of the United States at a disadvantage 
   176                  compared to the commerce of any foreign country. 
   177                  Section 338 also authorizes the President to suspend, 
   178                  revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under 
   179                  section 338 whenever the President deems that the 
   180                  public interests require such action. Further, section 
   181                  338 authorizes the President to exclude from 
   182                  importation articles of the foreign country if the 
   183                  foreign country maintains or increases the 
   184                  discrimination against the commerce of the United 
   185                  States and the President deems the exclusion to be 
   186                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   187                  of the United States.
   188  
   189                  10. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended 
   190                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the 
   191                  President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule 
   192                  of the United States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes 
   193                  affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, 
   194                  including the removal, modification, continuance, or 
   195                  imposition of any rate of duty or other import 
   196                  restriction.
   197  
   198                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   199                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   200                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   201                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   202                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   203                  follows:
   204

   206                  proclamation, certain products of Canada, as set forth 
   207                  in Annex I, Part A to this proclamation, imported into 
   208                  the United States shall no longer be subject to the 
   209                  additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent imposed 
   210                  pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended. In 
   211                  addition, certain products of Canada, as set forth in 
   212                  Annex I, Part B to this proclamation, imported into the 
   213                  United States shall be subject to the additional ad 
   214                  valorem duty of 50 percent imposed pursuant to 
   215                  Proclamation 11048, as amended. The duties imposed 
   216                  pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended, and as 
   217                  modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition 
   218                  to duties imposed pursuant to section 232 of the Trade 
   219                  Expansion Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1862). 
   220                  These changes shall be effective with respect to goods 
   221                  entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse 
   222                  for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   223                  October 30, 2026.
   224                      (2) The HTSUS is modified as provided in Annex II 
   225                  to this proclamation, effective with respect to goods 
   226                  entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse 
   227                  for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   228                  October 30, 2026, and the modifications shall continue 
   229                  in effect unless this action is expressly suspended, 
   230                  revoked, supplemented, amended, or terminated.
   231  
   232  [[Page 68863]]
   233  
   234                      (3) The head of each executive department and 
   235                  agency (agency) is authorized to and shall take all 
   236                  appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   237                  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency 
   238                  may, consistent with applicable law, including section 
   239                  301 of title 3, United States Code, redelegate the 
   240                  authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   241                  agency.
   242                      (4) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border 
   243                  Protection (CBP), in consultation with the Secretary of 
   244                  the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, and the United 
   245                  States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue 
   246                  such rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or 
   247                  determinations as may be necessary to implement this 
   248                  proclamation and is authorized to take any necessary 
   249                  measures to administer this proclamation.
   250                      (5) The Commissioner of CBP, in consultation with 
   251                  the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of 
   252                  Commerce, the United States Trade Representative, the 
   253                  Chairman of the United States International Trade 
   254                  Commission, and any other senior executive branch 
   255                  official the Commissioner of CBP deems appropriate, 
   256                  shall determine whether any additional modifications to 
   257                  the HTSUS are necessary to effectuate this proclamation 
   258                  and shall make such modifications to the HTSUS through 
   259                  notice in the Federal Register, including any technical 
   260                  or ministerial correction to the annexes to this 
   261                  proclamation.
   262                      (6) For any rule or regulation the Commissioner of 
   263                  CBP makes to implement this proclamation, the 
   264                  Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by 
   265                  law, obtain the approval of the President or the United 
   266                  States Trade Representative. The United States Trade 
   267                  Representative is delegated the President's approval 
   268                  authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).
   269                      (7) Any provision of previous proclamations and 
   270                  Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this 
   271                  proclamation is superseded to the extent of such 
   272                  inconsistency.
   273                      (8) If any provision of this proclamation or the 
   274                  application of any provision to any individual or 
   275                  circumstance is held to be invalid, the remainder of 
   276                  this proclamation and the application of its provisions 
   277                  to any other individuals or circumstances shall not be 
   278                  affected.
   279

   283                  United States of America the two hundred and fifty-

    64  Notice of Actions in Section 301 Investigations of Acts, 
    65  Policies, and Practices of Various Economies Related to the Failure of 
    66  Each Economy To Impose and Effectively Enforce a Prohibition on the 
    67  Importation of Goods Produced With Forced Labor
    68  
    69  AGENCY: Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR).
    70  
    71  ACTION: Notice of action.
    72  
    73  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    74  
    75  SUMMARY: The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) 
    76  has determined under Section 301(b) and Section 304(a) of the Trade Act 
    77  of 1974, as amended (Trade Act), that in each of 60 investigations, 
    78  certain of the acts, policies, and practices of the economy at issue 
    79  are actionable and that action by the United States is appropriate. In 
    80  accordance with the specific direction of the President, the Trade 
    81  Representative is taking actions in each of these investigations by 
    82  imposing tariffs on all products of the investigated economy, with 
    83  certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II to this notice 
    84  (Notice). Consistent with the specific direction of the President, for 
    85  an economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition, has 
    86  committed to impose and enforce such a prohibition through an Agreement 
    87  on Reciprocal Trade (ART), or has imposed a partial regime with the 
    88  effect of preventing the importation of certain forced labor goods, the 
    89  Trade Representative has determined 10 percent is the appropriate rate 
    90  of Section 301 duties, with specific economies subject to a 10 percent 
    91  rate net of a product's most-favored-nation (MFN) duty. For every other 
    92  economy, and in accordance with the specific direction of the 
    93  President, the Trade Representative has determined 12.5 percent is the 
    94  appropriate rate of Section 301 duty, with specific economies subject 
    95  to a 12.5 percent rate net of a product's MFN duty. The Trade 
    96  Representative has also determined, consistent with the specific 
    97  direction of the President, to establish, when feasible, tariff-rate 
    98  quotas (TRQs) for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia, based 
    99  on each economy's importation of U.S. inputs, to encourage the 
   100  importation by each of these economies of U.S. cotton and textile 
   101  goods, in order to reduce reliance on inputs from other sources that 
   102  are more likely to contain forced labor inputs.
   103  
   104  DATES: The additional rates of duty are applicable with respect to 
   105  products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse 
   106  for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, 
   107  except that goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in 
   108  transit on the final mode of transit before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   109  July 24, 2026, and entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse 
   110  for consumption before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026, shall 
   111  not be subject to such additional duty.
   112  
   113  FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: For general questions about this 
   114  Notice, contact Megan Grimball and Philip Butler, Chairs of the Section 
   115  301 Committee, at (202) 395-5725.
   116  
   117  SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
   118  
   119  I. Proceedings in the Investigations
   120  
   121      On March 12, 2026, the Trade Representative initiated 60 
   122  investigations related to the failure of various economies to each 
   123  impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of 
   124  goods produced wholly or in part with forced labor (forced labor import 
   125  prohibition), pursuant to 302(b)(1) of the Trade Act (19 U.S.C. 
   126  2412(b)(1)). See 91 FR 12884 (published March 17, 2026).
   127      On June 2, 2026, the Trade Representative determined that, in each 
   128  of the 60 investigations, certain of the acts, polices, and practices 
   129  of the economy at issue are actionable under sections 301(b) and 304(a) 
   130  of the Trade Act. The Trade Representative also issued a comprehensive 
   131  report, Acts, Policies, and Practices of Various Economies Related to 
   132  the Failure to Impose and Effectively Enforce a Prohibition on the 
   133  Importation of Goods Produced with Forced Labor (Report). Specifically, 
   134  the Trade Representative determined that:
   135       The following 54 economies have failed to impose and 
   136  effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced 
   137  with forced labor: Algeria; Angola; Argentina; Australia; the Bahamas; 
   138  Bahrain; Bangladesh; Brazil; Cambodia; Chile; China, People's Republic 
   139  of; Colombia; Costa Rica; Dominican Republic; Egypt; El Salvador; 
   140  Guatemala; Guyana; Honduras; Hong Kong, China; India; Iraq; Israel; 
   141  Japan; Jordan; Kazakhstan; Kuwait; Libya; Malaysia; Morocco; New 
   142  Zealand; Nicaragua; Nigeria; Norway; Oman; Peru; the Philippines; 
   143  Qatar; Russia; Saudi Arabia; Singapore; South Africa; South Korea; Sri 
   144  Lanka; Switzerland; Taiwan; Thailand; Trinidad and Tobago; 
   145  T[uuml]rkiye; United Arab Emirates; United Kingdom; Uruguay; Venezuela; 
   146  and Vietnam.
   147       The following six economies have failed to effectively 
   148  enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced 
   149  labor: Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and 
   150  Pakistan.
   151       All of the investigated economies have failed to impose a 
   152  forced labor import prohibition and to effectively enforce such a 
   153  prohibition (that is to say, all of the economies have failed to 
   154  satisfy both factors in these investigations).
   155      The Trade Representative proposed to determine that action is 
   156  appropriate in each investigation, and that appropriate action would 
   157  include tariffs on all products of an economy, with certain exemptions. 
   158  The Trade Representative also proposed a textile mechanism that would 
   159  allow for a certain volume of apparel and textile imports from certain 
   160  economies to enter the United States at a reduced Section 301 tariff 
   161  rate. See 91 FR 34272 (published June 5, 2026) (the June 5, 2026 FRN).
   162      The June 5, 2026 FRN invited public comments on the proposed 
   163  actions to be taken in each investigation. The June 5, 2026 FRN 
   164  proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a 
   165  forced labor import prohibition; has taken on commitments related to 
   166  forced labor import prohibitions through an ART; or has imposed a 
   167  partial regime with the effect of preventing the importation of certain 
   168  forced labor goods. The June 5, 2026 FRN proposed applying tariffs of 
   169  12.5 percent for every other economy. The tariff proposals in each 
   170  investigation included exemptions for certain goods, including 
   171  informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage, all articles 
   172  and parts of articles subject to tariffs under Section 232 of the Trade 
   173  Expansion Act of 1962, and certain products identified in Annex A to 
   174  the June 5, 2026 FRN.
   175      As explained in the June 5, 2026 FRN, the proposed exemptions 
   176  included: (a) raw materials that, if subject to the proposed additional 
   177  tariffs, could lead to the unavailability of domestic supply; (b) 
   178  products that could cause economy-wide disruptions if subject to 
   179  additional tariffs; (c) certain products that cannot be grown or 
   180  produced in sufficient quantities in the United States or obtained from 
   181  other sources; and (d) articles for which additional tariffs may not 
   182  contribute substantially to the elimination of the acts, policies, and 
   183  practices determined to be actionable in the investigations.
   184      Interested persons were invited to provide comments regarding the 
   185  scope
   186  
   187  [[Page 47319]]
   188  
   189  of tariff coverage (including the proposed excluded products identified 
   190  in Annex A to the June 5, 2026 FRN and the proposed textile mechanism. 
   191  With respect to the tariff proposals, the June 5, 2026 FRN stated that, 
   192  in considering whether certain articles should be subject to additional 
   193  duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act, USTR will consider the needs 
   194  of the U.S. economy. With respect to comments on the inclusion or 
   195  removal of particular tariff subheadings subject to the proposed 
   196  action, USTR requested that comments address specifically whether the 
   197  products under the tariff subheading are necessary raw materials that 
   198  if subject to the proposed tariff could lead to the unavailability of 
   199  domestic supply; whether additional tariffs would cause serious 
   200  dislocations in the supply of the products and could cause economy-wide 
   201  disruptions, or other similar factors; and whether imposing additional 
   202  tariffs on products under the tariff subheading would be practicable or 
   203  effective in obtaining the elimination of the investigated acts, 
   204  policies, and practices.
   205      USTR also requested public comments regarding the proposed actions, 
   206  including whether the products in Annex A to the June 5, 2026 FRN were 
   207  appropriately excluded; the level of the increase, if any, in the rate 
   208  of duty; whether differential tariff rates should be applied to an 
   209  economy where the economy has made a commitment to the United States to 
   210  impose and enforce a forced labor import prohibition, has imposed a 
   211  forced labor import prohibition, or has imposed a partial regime with 
   212  the effect of preventing the importation of certain forced labor goods; 
   213  and features of the proposed textile mechanism, including the U.S. and 
   214  foreign products to be covered, the relative market opportunities for 
   215  each side, and the tariff rate (if any) to be applied to products 
   216  subject to the mechanism, as well as whether a similar mechanism should 
   217  apply to any other product or sector.
   218      In response to the June 5, 2026 FRN, USTR received over 1,600 
   219  written comments. USTR and the Section 301 Committee held a three-day 
   220  public hearing on July 7, 8, and 9, 2026, regarding the proposed 
   221  actions. During the hearings, over 100 witnesses provided testimony and 
   222  responded to questions. Witnesses included representatives of the 
   223  governments of certain investigated economies, industry associations, 
   224  domestic producers, and non-governmental organizations. The public 
   225  submissions are available at: https://comments.ustr.gov/s/ at docket 
   226  numbers USTR-2026-0265 and USTR-2026-0266. Transcripts of the hearings 
   227  are available on USTR's website.
   228      Following government-to-government consultations pursuant to 
   229  Section 303 of the Trade Act and the publication of proposed actions in 
   230  the June 5, 2026 FRN, additional economies have imposed forced labor 
   231  import prohibitions--Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, 
   232  and Trinidad and Tobago; or undertaken commitments regarding forced 
   233  labor import prohibitions in an ART--Jordan.
   234  
   235  II. Determinations of Action
