    69                  Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
    70  
    71                  By the authority vested in me as President by the 
    72                  Constitution and the laws of the United States of 
    73                  America, including the International Emergency Economic 
    74                  Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) (IEEPA), the 
    75                  National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), 
    76                  section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 
    77                  U.S.C. 2483), and section 301 of title 3, United States 
    78                  Code, I hereby determine and order:
    79  
    80                  Section 1. Background. In Executive Order 14193 of 
    81                  February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties To Address the Flow 
    82                  of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border), I 
    83                  declared a national emergency arising from certain 
    84                  conditions, including the public health crisis caused 
    85                  by fentanyl and other illicit drugs, and the failure of 
    86                  Canada to do more to arrest, seize, detain, or 
    87                  otherwise intercept drug trafficking organizations, 
    88                  other drug or human traffickers, criminals at large, 
    89                  and illicit drugs. In that order, I found that those 
    90                  conditions constitute an unusual and extraordinary 
    91                  threat, which has its source in substantial part 
    92                  outside the United States, to the national security, 
    93                  foreign policy, and economy of the United States.
    94  
    95                  To deal with the emergency declared in Executive Order 
    96                  14193, I imposed an additional ad valorem rate of duty 
    97                  of 25 percent on certain articles that are products of 
    98                  Canada and an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 
    99                  percent on certain energy or energy resources that are 
   100                  products of Canada. In Executive Order 14231 of March 
   101                  6, 2025 (Amendment to Duties To Address the Flow of 
   102                  Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border), I provided 
   103                  that the additional ad valorem rates of duties under 
   104                  Executive Order 14193 do not apply to articles that are 
   105                  products of Canada that qualify for duty-free entry 
   106                  under the Agreement between the United States of 
   107                  America, United Mexican States, and Canada (USMCA), and 
   108                  I reduced the additional ad valorem rate of duty on 
   109                  potash from 25 percent to 10 percent.
   110  
   111                  Section 2(d) of Executive Order 14193 provides that 
   112                  ``[s]hould Canada retaliate against the United States . 
   113                  . . through import duties on United States exports to 
   114                  Canada or similar measures,'' I ``may increase or 
   115                  expand in scope the duties imposed . . . to ensure the 
   116                  efficacy of th[e] action'' taken in Executive Order 
   117                  14193. Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14193 provides 
   118                  that the Secretary of Homeland Security, in 
   119                  coordination with other senior officials, ``shall 
   120                  recommend additional action, if necessary, should the 
   121                  Government of Canada fail to take adequate steps to 
   122                  alleviate the illegal migration and illicit drug crises 
   123                  through cooperative enforcement actions.''
   124  
   125                  I have received additional information and 
   126                  recommendations from various senior officials 
   127                  regarding, among other things, Canada's lack of 
   128                  cooperation in stemming the flood of fentanyl and other 
   129                  illicit drugs across our northern border--including its 
   130                  failure to devote satisfactory resources to arrest, 
   131                  seize, detain, or otherwise intercept drug trafficking 
   132                  organizations, other drug or human traffickers, 
   133                  criminals at large, and illicit drugs--and Canada's 
   134                  efforts to retaliate against the United States in 
   135                  response to Executive Order 14193, as amended. After 
   136                  considering the additional information and 
   137                  recommendations that I have received, among other 
   138                  things, I have determined that, for the products of 
   139                  Canada that are subject to the additional ad valorem 
   140                  rate of duty of 25 percent, the additional ad valorem 
   141                  rate of duty shall increase from 25 percent to 35 
   142                  percent. In my judgment, this action is
   143  
   144  [[Page 37958]]
   145  
   146                  necessary and appropriate to deal with the emergency 
   147                  declared in Executive Order 14193.
   148  
   149                  Sec. 2. Implementation. (a) All articles that are 
   150                  subject to the additional ad valorem rate of duty of 25 
   151                  percent under Executive Order 14193, as amended, shall 
   152                  instead be subject to an additional ad valorem rate of 
   153                  duty of 35 percent. Accordingly, the Harmonized Tariff 
   154                  Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) shall be modified 
   155                  as provided in the Annex to this order.
   156  
   157                      (b) The changes set forth herein shall be effective 
   158                  with respect to goods entered for consumption, or 
   159                  withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 
   160                  12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on August 1, 2025.
   161                      (c) Nothing in this order shall be construed to 
   162                  alter or otherwise affect section 2(b) of Executive 
   163                  Order 14193 or section 2(a) or section 2(b) of 
   164                  Executive Order 14231.
   165                      (d) The stacking rules set out in Executive Order 
   166                  14289 of April 29, 2025 (Addressing Certain Tariffs on 
   167                  Imported Articles), and any subsequent order or 
   168                  proclamation addressing stacking of tariffs imposed 
   169                  under IEEPA, shall continue to apply to goods that are 
   170                  subject to subsection (a) of this section.
   171                      (e) The Secretary of Homeland Security, in 
   172                  consultation with the United States International Trade 
   173                  Commission, shall determine whether any additional 
   174                  modifications to the HTSUS are necessary to effectuate 
   175                  this order and may make such modifications through 
   176                  notice in the Federal Register.
   177  
   178                  Sec. 3. Transshipment. (a) All articles of Canada that 
   179                  do not qualify as originating under USMCA and are 
   180                  determined by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) 
   181                  to have been transshipped to evade applicable duties 
   182                  under section 2 of this order shall be subject to (i) 
   183                  an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 40 percent, in 
   184                  lieu of the additional ad valorem rate of duty 
   185                  applicable under section 2 of this order to goods of 
   186                  the country of origin; (ii) any other applicable or 
   187                  appropriate fine or penalty, including those assessed 
   188                  under 19 U.S.C. 1592; and (iii) any other United States 
   189                  duties, fees, taxes, exactions, or charges applicable 
   190                  to goods of the country of origin. CBP shall not allow, 
   191                  consistent with applicable law, for mitigation or 
   192                  remission of the penalties assessed on imports found to 
   193                  be transshipped to evade applicable duties.
   194  
   195                      (b) The Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of 
   196                  Homeland Security, acting through the Commissioner of 
   197                  CBP, in consultation with the United States Trade 
   198                  Representative, shall publish every 6 months a list of 
   199                  countries and specific facilities used in circumvention 
   200                  schemes, to inform public procurement, national 
   201                  security reviews, and commercial due diligence.
   202  
   203                  Sec. 4. Monitoring and Recommendations. (a) The 
   204                  Secretary of Homeland Security shall continue to 
   205                  monitor, and regularly consult with the Secretary of 
   206                  State, the Attorney General, the Assistant to the 
   207                  President for National Security Affairs, and the 
   208                  Assistant to the President for Homeland Security, on 
   209                  the situation at our northern border. The Secretary of 
   210                  Homeland Security shall inform the President of any 
   211                  circumstances that, in her opinion, might indicate the 
   212                  need for further action by the President. The Secretary 
   213                  of Homeland Security shall also inform the President of 
   214                  any circumstance that, in her opinion, might indicate 
   215                  that the Government of Canada has taken adequate steps 
   216                  to alleviate the emergency declared in Executive Order 
   217                  14193.
   218  
   219                      (b) The Secretary of Homeland Security, in 
   220                  coordination with the Secretary of State, the Attorney 
   221                  General, the Assistant to the President for National 
   222                  Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the President 
   223                  for Homeland Security, shall recommend additional 
   224                  action, if necessary, should the Government of Canada 
   225                  fail to take adequate steps to alleviate the illicit 
   226                  drug crisis or should the Government of Canada 
   227                  retaliate against the United States in response to the 
   228                  actions taken in Executive Order 14193 or any 
   229                  subsequent order issued to address the emergency 
   230                  declared in Executive Order 14193.
   231  
   232                  Sec. 5. Delegation. The Secretary of Homeland Security, 
   233                  in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the 
   234                  Attorney General, and the Secretary
   235  
   236  [[Page 37959]]
   237  
   238                  of Commerce, is hereby authorized to take such actions, 
   239                  including adopting rules and regulations, and to employ 
   240                  all powers granted to the President by IEEPA as may be 
   241                  necessary to implement this order. The Secretary of 
   242                  Homeland Security may, consistent with applicable law, 
   243                  redelegate any of these functions within the Department 
   244                  of Homeland Security. All executive departments and 
   245                  agencies shall take all appropriate measures within 
   246                  their authority to implement this order.

    27  
    28                  By the authority vested in me as President by the 
    29                  Constitution and the laws of the United States of 
    30                  America, including the International Emergency Economic 
    31                  Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.), the National 
    32                  Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), section 604 
    33                  of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 U.S.C. 2483), 
    34                  section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as 
    35                  amended (19 U.S.C. 1862), and section 301 of title 3, 
    36                  United States Code, it is hereby ordered:
    37  
    38                  Section 1. Purpose. The United States has imposed 
    39                  tariffs under various statutory authorities and through 
    40                  a number of Executive Orders and proclamations to 
    41                  protect national security and address unusual and 
    42                  extraordinary threats to the national security, foreign 
    43                  policy, and economy of the United States. Although each 
    44                  of these actions, as listed in section 2 of this order, 
    45                  serves separate and distinct policy purposes, I have 
    46                  now determined that, to the extent these tariffs apply 
    47                  to the same article, these tariffs should not all have 
    48                  a cumulative effect (or ``stack'' on top of one 
    49                  another) because the rate of duty resulting from such 
    50                  stacking exceeds what is necessary to achieve the 
    51                  intended policy goals. To avoid the cumulative effect 
    52                  of overlapping tariffs on certain articles, this order 
    53                  sets out the procedure for determining which of 
    54                  multiple tariffs shall apply to an article when that 
    55                  article is subject to more than one of the actions 
    56                  listed in section 2 of this order.
    57  
    58                  Sec. 2. Applicability. This order shall apply only to 
    59                  the administration of tariffs imposed through the 
    60                  following actions and subsequent amendments to those 
    61                  tariffs:
    62  
    63                      (a) Proclamation 10908 of March 26, 2025 (Adjusting 
    64                  Imports of Automobiles and Automobile Parts Into the 
    65                  United States);
    66                      (b) Executive Order 14193 of February 1, 2025 
    67                  (Imposing Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs 
    68                  Across Our Northern Border), as amended by Executive 
    69                  Order 14197 of February 3, 2025 (Progress on the 
    70                  Situation at Our Northern Border), Executive Order 
    71                  14226 of March 2, 2025 (Amendment to Duties To Address 
    72                  the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border), 
    73                  and Executive Order 14231 of March 6, 2025 (Amendment 
    74                  to Duties to Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across 
    75                  Our Northern Border);
    76                      (c) Executive Order 14194 of February 1, 2025 
    77                  (Imposing Duties To Address the Situation at Our 
    78                  Southern Border), as amended by Executive Order 14198 
    79                  of February 3, 2025 (Progress on the Situation at Our 
    80                  Southern Border), Executive Order 14227 of March 2, 
    81                  2025 (Amendment to Duties To Address the Situation at 
    82                  Our Southern Border), and Executive Order 14232 of 
    83                  March 6, 2025 (Amendment to Duties to Address the Flow 
    84                  of Illicit Drugs Across Our Southern Border);
    85                      (d) Proclamation 9704 of March 8, 2018 (Adjusting 
    86                  Imports of Aluminum Into the United States), as amended 
    87                  by Proclamation 9980 of January 24, 2020 (Adjusting 
    88                  Imports of Derivative Aluminum Articles and Derivative 
    89                  Steel Articles Into the United States), and 
    90                  Proclamation 10895 of February 10, 2025 (Adjusting 
    91                  Imports of Aluminum Into the United States); and
    92                      (e) Proclamation 9705 of March 8, 2018 (Adjusting 
    93                  Imports of Steel Into the United States), as amended by 
    94                  Proclamation 9980 of January 24, 2020 (Adjusting 
    95                  Imports of Derivative Aluminum Articles and Derivative 
    96                  Steel
    97  
    98  [[Page 18908]]
    99  
   100                  Articles Into the United States), and Proclamation 
   101                  10896 of February 10, 2025 (Adjusting Imports of Steel 
   102                  Into the United States).
   103  
   104                  Sec. 3. Non-Stacking of Tariff Measures. (a) 
   105                  Notwithstanding any provision of any action listed in 
   106                  section 2 of this order, tariffs for articles subject 
   107                  to tariffs under the actions listed in section 2 of 
   108                  this order shall apply as follows:
   109  
   110  (i) An article subject to tariffs pursuant to the action listed in section 
   111  (2)(a) of this order shall not be subject to additional tariffs on that 
   112  article pursuant to the actions listed in sections 2(b) through 2(e) of 
   113  this order.
   114  
   115  (ii) An article subject to tariffs pursuant to the actions listed in 
   116  section 2(b) or 2(c) of this order shall not be subject to additional 
   117  tariffs on that article pursuant to the actions listed in section 2(d) or 
   118  2(e) of this order.
   119  
   120  (iii) An article subject to tariffs pursuant to the actions listed in 
   121  section 2(d) of this order shall be subject to additional tariffs on that 
   122  article pursuant to the actions listed in section 2(e) of this order, 
   123  provided the article otherwise satisfies all conditions necessary for 
   124  application of those additional tariffs; likewise, an article subject to 
   125  tariffs pursuant to the actions listed in section 2(e) of this order shall 
   126  be subject to additional tariffs on that article pursuant to the actions 
   127  listed in section 2(d) of this order, provided the article otherwise 
   128  satisfies all conditions necessary for application of those additional 
   129  tariffs.
   130  
   131                      (b) Subsection (a) of this section shall not be 
   132                  construed to diminish the validity of any action listed 
   133                  in section 2 of this order. Each action listed in 
   134                  section 2 of this order remains independently valid and 
   135                  enforceable, except that the duty rates provided by 
   136                  these actions shall not be cumulative when the 
   137                  conditions outlined in subsection (a) of this section 
   138                  are met.
   139                      (c) If an imported article is subject to both a 
   140                  tariff imposed pursuant to subsection (a) of this 
   141                  section and one or more tariffs imposed pursuant to an 
   142                  action or actions not listed in section 2 of this 
   143                  order, then the tariff imposed on the article pursuant 
   144                  to subsection (a) of this section shall be cumulative 
   145                  with the tariff or tariffs imposed pursuant to the 
   146                  action or actions not listed in section 2 of this 
   147                  order.
   148  
   149                  Sec. 4. Non-applicability to Other Tariff Measures. (a) 
   150                  Nothing in this order shall be interpreted to alter or 
   151                  limit the application of any duties, taxes, fees, or 
   152                  exactions other than those imposed pursuant to the 
   153                  actions listed in section 2 of this order.
   154  
   155                      (b) Accordingly, an article that is subject to 
   156                  duties pursuant to an action listed in section 2 of 
   157                  this order may still be subject to other applicable 
   158                  duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges, such as, 
   159                  but not limited to, those set forth in column 1 of the 
   160                  Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States 
   161                  (HTSUS); duties imposed pursuant to section 301 of the 
   162                  Trade Act of 1974, as amended; duties imposed pursuant 
   163                  to Executive Order 14195 of February 1, 2025 (Imposing 
   164                  Duties To Address the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in 
   165                  the People's Republic of China), as amended; and 
   166                  antidumping and countervailing duties.
   167  
   168                  Sec. 5. Implementation. (a) The Secretary of Homeland 
   169                  Security, acting through the Commissioner of U.S. 
   170                  Customs and Border Protection and in consultation with 
   171                  the Secretary of the Treasury, shall take all necessary 
   172                  steps to update guidance, systems, and enforcement 
   173                  mechanisms, including to revise, suspend, or rescind 
   174                  any regulations that may be inconsistent with this 
   175                  order, to reflect the policy set forth in this order.
   176  
   177                      (b) The Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of 
   178                  Homeland Security, in coordination with the Secretary 
   179                  of the Treasury and the United States Trade 
   180                  Representative, shall provide additional guidance as 
   181                  necessary to ensure consistent interpretation and 
   182                  application of the policy set forth in this order.
   183                      (c) The Secretary of Homeland Security is 
   184                  authorized to determine whether changes to the HTSUS 
   185                  are necessary and to coordinate with the Chair
   186  
   187  [[Page 18909]]
   188  
   189                  of the United States International Trade Commission to 
   190                  implement all necessary changes to execute this order.
   191                      (d) Any changes to the HTSUS necessary to comply 
   192                  with this order shall be made not later than 12:01 a.m. 
   193                  eastern daylight time on May 16, 2025. This order shall 
   194                  apply retroactively to all entries of merchandise 
   195                  subject to any applicable tariffs outlined in section 2 
   196                  of this order and made on or after March 4, 2025. Any 
   197                  refunds will be processed pursuant to applicable laws 
   198                  and U.S. Customs and Border Protection's standard 
   199                  procedures for such refunds.
   200  
   201                  Sec. 6. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order 
   202                  shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
   203  
   204  (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or 
   205  the head thereof; or
   206  
   207  (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
   208  relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
   209  
   210                      (b) This order shall be implemented consistent with 
   211                  applicable law and subject to the availability of 
   212                  appropriations.
   213                      (c) This order is not intended to, and does not, 
   214                  create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, 
   215                  enforceable at law or in equity by any party against 
   216                  the United States, its departments, agencies, or 
   217                  entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any 
   218                  other person.

    26  Ending Certain Tariff Actions
    27  
    28                  By the authority vested in me as President by the 
    29                  Constitution and the laws of the United States of 
    30                  America, including the International Emergency Economic 
    31                  Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) (IEEPA), the 
    32                  National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), 
    33                  section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (19 
    34                  U.S.C. 2483), and section 301 of title 3, United States 
    35                  Code, it is hereby ordered:
    36  
    37                  Section 1. Background. In Executive Order 14193 of 
    38                  February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties To Address the Flow 
    39                  of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border), as 
    40                  amended; Executive Order 14194 of February 1, 2025 
    41                  (Imposing Duties To Address the Situation at Our 
    42                  Southern Border), as amended; Executive Order 14195 of 
    43                  February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties To Address the 
    44                  Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic 
    45                  of China), as amended; Executive Order 14245 of March 
    46                  24, 2025 (Imposing Tariffs on Countries Importing 
    47                  Venezuelan Oil); Executive Order 14257 of April 2, 2025 
    48                  (Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify 
    49                  Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent 
    50                  Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits), as amended; 
    51                  Executive Order 14323 of July 30, 2025 (Addressing 
    52                  Threats to the United States by the Government of 
    53                  Brazil), as amended; Executive Order 14329 of August 6, 
    54                  2025 (Addressing Threats to the United States by the 
    55                  Government of the Russian Federation), as amended; 
    56                  Executive Order 14380 of January 29, 2026 (Addressing 
    57                  Threats to the United States by the Government of 
    58                  Cuba); and Executive Order 14382 of February 6, 2026 
    59                  (Addressing Threats to the United States by the 
    60                  Government of Iran), I declared or described national 
    61                  emergencies with respect to unusual and extraordinary 
    62                  threats to the national security, foreign policy, or 
    63                  economy of the United States and took actions to deal 
    64                  with those threats, including by imposing, pursuant to 
    65                  IEEPA, additional ad valorem duties on certain imports 
    66                  of certain foreign trading partners.
    67  
    68                  In light of recent events, the additional ad valorem 
    69                  duties imposed pursuant to IEEPA in Executive Order 
    70                  14193, as amended; Executive Order 14194, as amended; 
    71                  Executive Order 14195, as amended; Executive Order 
    72                  14245; Executive Order 14257, as amended; Executive 
    73                  Order 14323, as amended; Executive Order 14329, as 
    74                  amended; Executive Order 14380; and Executive Order 
    75                  14382 shall no longer be in effect and, as soon as 
    76                  practicable, shall no longer be collected. All other 
    77                  actions, including any other action taken to address 
    78                  the national emergencies declared or described in 
    79                  Executive Order 14193, Executive Order 14194, Executive 
    80                  Order 14195, Executive Order 14245, Executive Order 
    81                  14257, Executive Order 14323, Executive Order 14329, 
    82                  Executive Order 14380, and Executive Order 14382, that 
    83                  do not impose additional ad valorem duties under IEEPA 
    84                  or involve steps necessary to implement the imposition 
    85                  of additional ad valorem duties imposed under IEEPA 
    86                  shall not be affected by this order. The national 
    87                  emergencies declared or described in Executive Order 
    88                  14193, Executive Order 14194, Executive Order 14195, 
    89                  Executive Order 14245, Executive Order 14257, Executive 
    90                  Order 14323, Executive Order 14329, Executive Order 
    91                  14380, and Executive Order 14382 or subsequent orders 
    92                  remain in effect and shall not be affected by this 
    93                  order.
    94  
    95                  Sec. 2. Implementation. (a) To effectuate the 
    96                  terminations of the actions described in section 1 of 
    97                  this order, the head of each executive department and 
    98                  agency (agency) is authorized to and shall take all 
    99                  appropriate steps
   100  
   101  [[Page 9438]]
   102  
   103                  to end the additional ad valorem duties imposed under 
   104                  IEEPA in Executive Order 14193, as amended; Executive 
   105                  Order 14194, as amended; Executive Order 14195, as 
   106                  amended; Executive Order 14245; Executive Order 14257, 
   107                  as amended; Executive Order 14323, as amended; 
   108                  Executive Order 14329, as amended; Executive Order 
   109                  14380; and Executive Order 14382. The head of each 
   110                  agency shall immediately begin taking steps to 
   111                  effectuate this order and, as soon as practicable, 
   112                  terminate the collection of the additional ad valorem 
   113                  duties described in section 1 of this order. The head 
   114                  of each agency may, consistent with applicable law, 
   115                  including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
   116                  redelegate the authority to take such appropriate steps 
   117                  within the agency.
   118  
   119                      (b) The Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of 
   120                  Homeland Security, and the United States Trade 
   121                  Representative, as appropriate and in consultation with 
   122                  the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, 
   123                  the Chair of the United States International Trade 
   124                  Commission, and any other senior official they deem 
   125                  appropriate, shall determine whether modifications to 
   126                  the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States are 
   127                  necessary to effectuate this order and may make such 
   128                  modifications through notice in the Federal Register.
   129                      (c) The Executive Order of February 20, 2026 
   130                  (Continuing the Suspension of Duty-Free De Minimis 
   131                  Treatment for All Countries), and the Proclamation of 
   132                  February 20, 2026 (Imposing a Temporary Import 
   133                  Surcharge to Address Fundamental International Payments 
   134                  Problems), are unaffected by this order.
   135                      (d) This order affects only the additional ad 
   136                  valorem duties imposed under IEEPA pursuant to the 
   137                  Executive Orders described in section 1 of this order. 
   138                  This order does not affect any other duties, including 
   139                  duties imposed under section 232 of the Trade Expansion 
   140                  Act of 1962, as amended, 19 U.S.C. 1862, and section 
   141                  301 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended, 19 U.S.C. 
   142                  2411.
   143  
   144                  Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order 
   145                  shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
   146  
   147  (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or 
   148  the head thereof; or
   149  
   150  (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
   151  relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
   152  
   153                      (b) This order shall be implemented consistent with 
   154                  applicable law and subject to the availability of 
   155                  appropriations.
   156  
   157  [[Page 9439]]
   158  
   159                      (c) This order is not intended to, and does not, 
   160                  create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, 
   161                  enforceable at law or in equity by any party against 
   162                  the United States, its departments, agencies, or 
   163                  entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any 
   164                  other person.
   165                      (d) The costs for publication of this order shall 
   166                  be borne by the Department of Homeland Security.

    65                  Proclamation 11012 of February 20, 2026
    66  
    67                  
    68  Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address 
    69                  Fundamental International Payments Problems
    70  
    71                  By the President of the United States of America
    72  
    73                  A Proclamation
    74  
    75                  1. The United States plays a pivotal role in shaping 
    76                  the global economy. At the same time, the United States 
    77                  faces various threats to its own economy and national 
    78                  interests. Sometimes, the United States faces 
    79                  fundamental international payments problems, such as 
    80                  large and serious balance-of-payments deficits, an 
    81                  imminent and significant depreciation of its currency 
    82                  in foreign exchange markets, or an international 
    83                  balance-of-payments disequilibrium. These problems can, 
    84                  among other things, endanger the ability of the United 
    85                  States to finance its spending, erode investor 
    86                  confidence in the economy, and distress the financial 
    87                  markets.
    88  
    89                  2. Special import measures to restrict imports, such as 
    90                  surcharges and quotas, are key tools to protect the 
    91                  economy and national security of the United States, 
    92                  and, in certain circumstances, they are required to 
    93                  deal with fundamental international payments problems.
    94  
    95                  3. Given the gravity of fundamental international 
    96                  payments problems and the importance of import 
    97                  restrictions as economic, national security, and 
    98                  foreign policy tools, Federal law, including section 
    99                  122 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2132) (section 
   100                  122), empowers the President to take action through 
   101                  surcharges and other special import restrictions to 
   102                  address fundamental international payments problems.
   103  
   104                  4. I have received certain requested information and 
   105                  opinions from senior officials on whether any 
   106                  fundamental international payments problems exist and 
   107                  the extent to which such problems could impair United 
   108                  States national interests, including economic and 
   109                  national security interests. The information and 
   110                  opinions discuss, among other things, the state of the 
   111                  balance of payments of the United States, the standing 
   112                  of the United States dollar in foreign exchange 
   113                  markets, and the state of international balances of 
   114                  payments. I have also received opinions and 
   115                  recommendations from senior officials on whether 
   116                  special import measures to restrict imports are 
   117                  required to address any fundamental international 
   118                  payments problems. These opinions address, among other 
   119                  things, whether a surcharge in the form of ad valorem 
   120                  duties is required to restrict imports to deal with 
   121                  large and serious United States balance-of-payments 
   122                  deficits, to prevent an imminent and significant 
   123                  depreciation of the United States dollar in foreign 
   124                  exchange markets, or to cooperate with other countries 
   125                  in correcting an international balance-of-payments 
   126                  disequilibrium.
   127  
   128                  5. These senior officials have informed me that 
   129                  fundamental international payments problems within the 
   130                  meaning of section 122 exist and that special import 
   131                  measures to restrict imports are required to address 
   132                  these problems. Specifically, my advisors have 
   133                  determined that an import surcharge in the form of ad 
   134                  valorem duties is required to deal with large and 
   135                  serious United States balance-of-payments deficits. My 
   136                  advisors have also opined that certain products should 
   137                  not be subject to the surcharge because of the needs of 
   138                  the United States economy and that the recommended 
   139                  exceptions are consistent with the limitations of 
   140                  section 122, the purposes of section 122, and the 
   141                  national interest of the United States.
   142  
   143  [[Page 9340]]
   144  
   145                  6. Among other things, I have been informed by my 
   146                  advisors that the United States balance-of-payments 
   147                  position, under any reasonable understanding of the 
   148                  term in the context of section 122, is currently a 
   149                  large and serious deficit. My advisors have studied 
   150                  different methods of evaluating balance-of-payments 
   151                  deficits, including calculations based on current-
   152                  account statistics. In my advisors' opinions, under any 
   153                  of these methods, the United States balance-of-payments 
   154                  position is a large and serious deficit.
   155  
   156                  7. For instance, my advisors have informed me that the 
   157                  United States runs a deficit in selling goods and 
   158                  services overseas, as reported by the United States 
   159                  Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) in the ``balance on 
   160                  goods and services''; has recently reflected quarterly 
   161                  deficits in its return on investment or labor, as 
   162                  reported by the BEA in the ``balance on primary 
   163                  income''; and runs a deficit in voluntary transfers, 
   164                  such as remittances, as reported by the BEA in the 
   165                  ``balance on secondary income.'' In other words, the 
   166                  United States runs a trade deficit, does not currently 
   167                  make a net income from the capital and labor that it 
   168                  deploys abroad, and experiences more transfer payments, 
   169                  on net, flowing out of the country than into the 
   170                  country.
   171  
   172                  8. As my advisors have informed me, the United States 
   173                  runs a substantial trade deficit. The large, 
   174                  persistent, and serious annual United States goods 
   175                  trade deficit has grown by over 40 percent in the past 
   176                  5 years alone, reaching $1.2 trillion in 2024. In 2025, 
   177                  the United States goods trade deficit remained at 
   178                  approximately $1.2 trillion. The effects of this 
   179                  deficit are serious, and this deficit contributes to 
   180                  the fundamental international payments problems facing 
   181                  the United States.
   182  
   183                  9. As my advisors have also informed me, the annual 
   184                  balance on the United States primary income turned 
   185                  negative for the first time since at least 1960 in 
   186                  2024. From 1960 to 2023, the United States ran a 
   187                  surplus in its annual balance on primary income. That 
   188                  positive balance on primary income served as a 
   189                  stabilizing force for the United States balance-of-
   190                  payments position even in the face of large and 
   191                  persistent trade deficits. In 2024, however, the 
   192                  balance on primary income turned negative and thus 
   193                  ceased to serve as a counterweight to the trade deficit 
   194                  in the United States current account. Indeed, in 2024, 
   195                  the United States maintained a current account deficit 
   196                  of 4.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), almost 
   197                  double the current account deficit of approximately 2.0 
   198                  percent that prevailed between 2013 and 2019, and 
   199                  larger than that which prevailed from 2019 to 2023. As 
   200                  a share of GDP, the staggering deficit of 4.0 percent 
   201                  represented the biggest annual current account deficit 
   202                  since 2008.
   203  
   204                  10. As my advisors have also informed me, the net 
   205                  international-investment position of the United States 
   206                  is in an ongoing decline. According to the BEA, at the 
   207                  end of 2024, the net international-investment position 
   208                  of the United States, as a share of GDP, was negative 
   209                  90 percent, a sharp deterioration from the average of 
   210                  negative 41 percent in the decade between 2010 and 
   211                  2020. In my advisors' view, this is a highly atypical 
   212                  position for a country, particularly the United States. 
   213                  Indeed, both in terms of United States dollars and as a 
   214                  share of GDP, this represents one of the most negative 
   215                  net international-investment positions of any developed 
   216                  country. Because the current account is one of the 
   217                  primary drivers of changes in the net international-
   218                  investment position, the atypically large negative net 
   219                  international-investment position of the United States 
   220                  shows that the United States balance-of-payments 
   221                  deficit is large and serious.
   222  
   223                  11. Further, as my advisors have informed me, the 
   224                  balance on secondary income of the United States has 
   225                  been persistently in a deficit since the 1960s.
   226  
   227                  12. According to my advisors, an import surcharge in 
   228                  the form of ad valorem duties is required to address 
   229                  these fundamental international payments problems. In 
   230                  my advisors' opinions, imposing an import surcharge 
   231                  would deal with the large and serious United States 
   232                  balance-of-payments deficit. My advisors have further 
   233                  recommended that certain products should not be subject 
   234                  to the surcharge because of the needs of the United 
   235                  States economy
   236  
   237  [[Page 9341]]
   238  
   239                  and have opined that a surcharge with certain 
   240                  exceptions would more effectively deal with the 
   241                  balance-of-payments deficit than would a surcharge 
   242                  without the exceptions.
   243  
   244                  13. After considering the information, opinions, and 
   245                  recommendations that have been provided to me by senior 
   246                  officials, among other relevant information and 
   247                  considerations, I find that fundamental international 
   248                  payments problems within the meaning of section 122 
   249                  exist; that those problems significantly harm United 
   250                  States national interests, including economic and 
   251                  national security interests; and that special measures 
   252                  to restrict imports are required to address those 
   253                  problems, as authorized by section 122. Specifically, I 
   254                  find that a surcharge in the form of ad valorem duties 
   255                  on certain imports is required to deal with the United 
   256                  States' large and serious balance-of-payments deficit. 
   257                  Accordingly, I impose, for a period of 150 days, a 
   258                  temporary import surcharge of 10 percent ad valorem, as 
   259                  described below, on articles imported into the United 
   260                  States, effective February 24, 2026.
   261  
   262                  14. Because of the needs of the United States economy, 
   263                  I determine that the surcharge imposed in this 
   264                  proclamation shall not apply to the following products, 
   265                  as further detailed in Annexes I and II to this 
   266                  proclamation:
   267  
   268                  (a) certain critical minerals;
   269  
   270                  (b) metals used in currency and bullion;
   271  
   272                  (c) energy and energy products;
   273  
   274                  (d) natural resources and fertilizers that cannot be 
   275                  grown, mined, or otherwise produced in the United 
   276                  States or grown, mined, or otherwise produced in 
   277                  sufficient quantities to meet domestic demand;
   278  
   279                  (e) certain agricultural products, including beef, 
   280                  tomatoes, and oranges;
   281  
   282                  (f) pharmaceuticals and pharmaceutical ingredients;
   283  
   284                  (g) certain electronics;
   285  
   286                  (h) passenger vehicles, certain light trucks, certain 
   287                  medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, buses, and certain 
   288                  parts of passenger vehicles, light trucks, medium- and 
   289                  heavy-duty vehicles, and buses;
   290  
   291                  (i) certain aerospace products;
   292  
   293                  (j) information materials, donations, and accompanied 
   294                  baggage;
   295  
   296                  (k) all articles and parts of articles currently or 
   297                  that later become subject to additional import 
   298                  restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232 of the 
   299                  Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 
   300                  1862) (section 232);

   400  fees, exactions, and charges applicable to such products.
   401  
   402  (4) The surcharge imposed in this proclamation shall not apply in addition 
   403  to tariffs imposed under section 232. To the extent a tariff imposed under 
   404  section 232 applies to part of an import, the surcharge imposed in this 
   405  proclamation shall apply to the part of the import to which section 232 
   406  tariffs do not apply but shall not apply to the part of the import to which 
   407  section 232 tariffs do apply.
   408  
   409  (5) The surcharge imposed in this proclamation shall be treated as a 
   410  regular customs duty.
   411  
   412  (6) Any article subject to the surcharge imposed in this proclamation, 
   413  except those articles eligible for admission under ``domestic status'' as 
   414  described in 19 CFR 146.43, that is subject to the surcharge imposed in 
   415  this proclamation and that is admitted into a United States foreign trade 
   416  zone on or after the effective date of this proclamation must be
   417  
   418  [[Page 9343]]
   419  
   420  admitted as ``privileged foreign status,'' as described in 19 CFR 146.41, 
   421  and will be subject upon entry for consumption to any ad valorem rate of 
   422  duty related to the classification under the applicable HTSUS subheading.

   424  (7) The HTSUS shall be modified as provided in Annex I to this 
   425  proclamation. The modifications shall be effective with respect to goods 
   426  entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or 
   427  after 12:01 a.m. eastern standard time on February 24, 2026, and shall

   434  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   435  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency may, consistent with 
   436  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
   437  redelegate the authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   438  agency.

   440  (9) The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative), in 
   441  consultation with any senior official he deems appropriate, shall monitor 
   442  and review the status of conditions related to the fundamental 
   443  international payments problems of the United States, the effect of the 
   444  surcharge imposed in this proclamation, and any factors he deems relevant.

   446  circumstance that, in the Trade Representative's opinion, might indicate

   448  And the Trade Representative shall inform the President of any circumstance 
   449  that, in the Trade Representative's opinion, might indicate that the

   453  (10) The Trade Representative, in consultation with the Chair of the United 
   454  States International Trade Commission and the Commissioner of U.S. Customs 
   455  and Border Protection (CBP), shall determine whether any additional

   464  (12) (a) Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that

   466  inconsistency. If any provision of this proclamation or the application of

   471                  (b) If any exception to the surcharge imposed in this

   474                  be treated as invalid. The surcharge imposed in this

   485                  invalidated part of the exception applied before its

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

    30  Imposing Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit 
    31                  Drugs Across Our Northern Border
    32  
    33                  By the authority vested in me as President by the 
    34                  Constitution and the laws of the United States of 
    35                  America, including the International Emergency Economic 
    36                  Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) (IEEPA), the 
    37                  National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.) 
    38                  (NEA), section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended 
    39                  (19 U.S.C. 2483), and section 301 of title 3, United 
    40                  States Code,
    41  
    42                  I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of 
    43                  America, find that the sustained influx of illicit 
    44                  opioids and other drugs has profound consequences on 
    45                  our Nation, endangering lives and putting a severe 
    46                  strain on our healthcare system, public services, and 
    47                  communities.
    48  
    49                  This challenge threatens the fabric of our society. 
    50                  Gang members, smugglers, human traffickers, and illicit 
    51                  drugs of all kinds have poured across our borders and 
    52                  into our communities. Canada has played a central role 
    53                  in these challenges, including by failing to devote 
    54                  sufficient attention and resources or meaningfully 
    55                  coordinate with United States law enforcement partners 
    56                  to effectively stem the tide of illicit drugs.
    57  
    58                  Drug trafficking organizations (DTOs) are the world's 
    59                  leading producers of fentanyl, methamphetamine, 
    60                  cocaine, and other illicit drugs, and they cultivate, 
    61                  process, and distribute massive quantities of narcotics 
    62                  that fuel addiction and violence in communities across 
    63                  the United States. These DTOs often collaborate with 
    64                  transnational cartels to smuggle illicit drugs into the 
    65                  United States, utilizing clandestine airstrips, 
    66                  maritime routes, and overland corridors.
    67  
    68                  The challenges at our southern border are foremost in 
    69                  the public consciousness, but our northern border is 
    70                  not exempt from these issues. Criminal networks are 
    71                  implicated in human trafficking and smuggling 
    72                  operations, enabling unvetted illegal migration across 
    73                  our northern border. There is also a growing presence 
    74                  of Mexican cartels operating fentanyl and nitazene 
    75                  synthesis labs in Canada. The flow of illicit drugs 
    76                  like fentanyl to the United States through both illicit 
    77                  distribution networks and international mail--due, in 
    78                  the case of the latter, to the existing administrative 
    79                  exemption from duty and taxes, also known as de 
    80                  minimis, under section 1321 of title 19, United States 
    81                  Code--has created a public health crisis in the United 
    82                  States, as outlined in the Presidential Memorandum of 
    83                  January 20, 2025 (America First Trade Policy) and 
    84                  Executive Order 14157 of January 20, 2025 (Designating 
    85                  Cartels and Other Organizations as Foreign Terrorist 
    86                  Organizations and Specially Designated Global 
    87                  Terrorists). With respect to smuggling of illicit drugs 
    88                  across our northern border, Canada's Financial 
    89                  Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre recently 
    90                  published a study on the laundering of proceeds of 
    91                  illicit synthetic opioids, which recognized Canada's 
    92                  heightened domestic production of fentanyl, largely 
    93                  from British Columbia, and its growing footprint within 
    94                  international narcotics distribution. Despite a North 
    95                  American dialogue on the public health impacts of 
    96                  illicit drugs since 2016, Canadian officials have 
    97                  acknowledged that the problem has only grown. And while 
    98                  U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) within the 
    99                  Department of Homeland Security seized, comparatively, 
   100                  much less fentanyl from Canada than from Mexico last 
   101                  year, fentanyl is so potent that even a very small 
   102                  parcel of the drug can cause many deaths and
   103  
   104  [[Page 9114]]
   105  
   106                  destruction to America families. In fact, the amount of 
   107                  fentanyl that crossed the northern border last year 
   108                  could kill 9.5 million Americans.
   109  
   110                  Immediate action is required to finally end this public 
   111                  health crisis and national emergency, which will not 
   112                  happen unless the compliance and cooperation of Canada 
   113                  is assured.
   114  
   115                  I hereby determine and order:
   116  
   117                  Section 1. (a) As President of the United States, my 
   118                  highest duty is the defense of the country and its 
   119                  citizens. A Nation without borders is not a nation at 
   120                  all. I will not stand by and allow our sovereignty to 
   121                  be eroded, our laws to be trampled, our citizens to be 
   122                  endangered, or our borders to be disrespected anymore.
   123  
   124                  I previously declared a national emergency with respect 
   125                  to the grave threat to the United States posed by the 
   126                  influx of illegal aliens and illicit drugs into the 
   127                  United States in Proclamation 10886 of January 20, 2025 
   128                  (Declaring a National Emergency at the Southern 
   129                  Border). Pursuant to the NEA, I hereby expand the scope 
   130                  of the national emergency declared in that Proclamation 
   131                  to cover the threat to the safety and security of 
   132                  Americans, including the public health crisis of deaths 
   133                  due to the use of fentanyl and other illicit drugs, and 
   134                  the failure of Canada to do more to arrest, seize, 
   135                  detain, or otherwise intercept DTOs, other drug and 
   136                  human traffickers, criminals at large, and drugs. In 
   137                  addition, this failure to act on the part of Canada 
   138                  constitutes an unusual and extraordinary threat, which 
   139                  has its source in substantial part outside the United 
   140                  States, to the national security and foreign policy of 
   141                  the United States. I hereby declare and reiterate a 
   142                  national emergency under the NEA and IEEPA to deal with 
   143                  that threat. This national emergency requires decisive 
   144                  and immediate action, and I have decided to impose, 
   145                  consistent with law, ad valorem tariffs on articles 
   146                  that are products of Canada set forth in this order. In 
   147                  doing so, I invoke my authority under section 
   148                  1702(a)(1)(B) of IEEPA, and specifically find that 
   149                  action under other authority to impose tariffs is 
   150                  inadequate to address this unusual and extraordinary 
   151                  threat.
   152  
   153                  Sec. 2. (a) All articles that are products of Canada as 
   154                  defined by the Federal Register notice described in 
   155                  subsection (e) of this section (Federal Register 
   156                  notice), and except for those products described in 
   157                  subsection (b) of this section, shall be, consistent 
   158                  with law, subject to an additional 25 percent ad 
   159                  valorem rate of duty. Such rate of duty shall apply 
   160                  with respect to goods entered for consumption, or 
   161                  withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 
   162                  12:01 a.m. eastern time on February 4, 2025, except 
   163                  that goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   164                  warehouse for consumption, after such time that were 
   165                  loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading or in 
   166                  transit on the final mode of transport prior to entry 
   167                  into the United States before 12:01 a.m. eastern time 
   168                  on February 1, 2025, shall not be subject to such 
   169                  additional duty, only if the importer certifies to CBP 
   170                  as specified in the Federal Register notice.
   171  
   172                      (b) With respect to energy or energy resources, as 
   173                  defined in section 8 of Executive Order 14156 of 
   174                  January 20, 2025 (Declaring a National Energy 
   175                  Emergency), and as otherwise included in the Federal 
   176                  Register notice, such articles that are products of 
   177                  Canada as defined by the Federal Register notice shall 
   178                  be, consistent with law, subject to an additional 10 
   179                  percent ad valorem rate of duty. Such rate of duty 
   180                  shall apply with respect to goods entered for 
   181                  consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for 
   182                  consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   183                  February 4, 2025, except that goods entered for 
   184                  consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for 
   185                  consumption, after such time that were loaded onto a 
   186                  vessel at the port of loading or in transit on the 
   187                  final mode of transport prior to entry into the United 
   188                  States before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on February 1, 
   189                  2025, shall not be subject to such additional duty, 
   190                  only if the importer certifies to CBP as specified in 
   191                  the Federal Register notice.
   192                      (c) The rates of duty established by this order are 
   193                  in addition to any other duties, fees, exactions, or 
   194                  charges applicable to such imported articles.
   195  
   196  [[Page 9115]]
   197  
   198                      (d) Should Canada retaliate against the United 
   199                  States in response to this action through import duties 
   200                  on United States exports to Canada or similar measures, 
   201                  the President may increase or expand in scope the 
   202                  duties imposed under this order to ensure the efficacy 
   203                  of this action.
   204                      (e) In order to establish the duty rate on imports 
   205                  of articles that are products of Canada, the Secretary 
   206                  of Homeland Security shall determine the modifications 
   207                  necessary to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the 
   208                  United States (HTSUS) in order to effectuate this order 
   209                  consistent with law and shall make such modifications 
   210                  to the HTSUS through notice in the Federal Register. 
   211                  The modifications made to the HTSUS by this notice 
   212                  shall be effective with respect to goods entered for 
   213                  consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for 
   214                  consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   215                  February 4, 2025, and shall continue in effect until 
   216                  such actions are expressly reduced, modified, or 
   217                  terminated.
   218                      (f) Articles that are products of Canada, except 
   219                  those that are eligible for admission under ``domestic 
   220                  status'' as defined in 19 CFR 146.43, which are subject 
   221                  to the duties imposed by this order and are admitted 
   222                  into a United States foreign trade zone on or after 
   223                  12:01 a.m. eastern time on February 4, 2025, except as 
   224                  otherwise noted in subsections (a) and (b) of this 
   225                  section, must be admitted as ``privileged foreign 
   226                  status'' as defined in 19 CFR 146.41. Such articles 
   227                  will be subject upon entry for consumption to the rates 
   228                  of duty related to the classification under the 
   229                  applicable HTSUS subheading in effect at the time of 
   230                  admittance into the United States foreign trade zone.
   231                      (g) No drawback shall be available with respect to 
   232                  the duties imposed pursuant to this order.
   233                      (h) For avoidance of doubt, duty-free de minimis 
   234                  treatment under 19 U.S.C. 1321 shall not be available 
   235                  for the articles described in subsection (a) and 
   236                  subsection (b) of this section.
   237                      (i) Any prior Presidential Proclamation, Executive 
   238                  Order, or other Presidential directive or guidance 
   239                  related to trade with Canada that is inconsistent with 
   240                  the direction in this order is hereby terminated, 
   241                  suspended, or modified to the extent necessary to give 
   242                  full effect to this order.
   243                      (j) The articles described in subsection (a) and 
   244                  subsection (b) of this section shall exclude those 
   245                  encompassed by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b).
   246  
   247                  Sec. 3. (a) The Secretary of Homeland Security shall 
   248                  regularly consult with the Secretary of State, the 
   249                  Attorney General, the Assistant to the President for 
   250                  National Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the 
   251                  President for Homeland Security on the situation at our 
   252                  northern border. The Secretary of Homeland Security 
   253                  shall inform the President of any circumstances that, 
   254                  in the opinion of the Secretary of Homeland Security, 
   255                  indicate that the Government of Canada has taken 
   256                  adequate steps to alleviate this public health crisis 
   257                  through cooperative enforcement actions. Upon the 
   258                  President's determination of sufficient action to 
   259                  alleviate the crisis, the tariffs described in section 
   260                  2 of this order shall be removed.
   261  
   262                      (b) The Secretary of Homeland Security, in 
   263                  coordination with the Secretary of State, the Attorney 
   264                  General, the Assistant to the President for National 
   265                  Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the President 
   266                  for Homeland Security, shall recommend additional 
   267                  action, if necessary, should the Government of Canada 
   268                  fail to take adequate steps to alleviate the illegal 
   269                  migration and illicit drug crises through cooperative 
   270                  enforcement actions.
   271  
   272                  Sec. 4. The Secretary of Homeland Security, in 
   273                  consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the 
   274                  Attorney General, and the Secretary of Commerce, is 
   275                  hereby authorized to take such actions, including 
   276                  adopting rules and regulations, and to employ all 
   277                  powers granted to the President by IEEPA as may be 
   278                  necessary to implement this order. The Secretary of 
   279                  Homeland Security may, consistent with applicable law, 
   280                  redelegate any of these functions within the Department 
   281                  of Homeland Security. All executive departments
   282  
   283  [[Page 9116]]
   284  
   285                  and agencies shall take all appropriate measures within 
   286                  their authority to implement this order.
   287  
   288                  Sec. 5. The Secretary of Homeland Security, in 
   289                  coordination with the Secretary of the Treasury, the 
   290                  Attorney General, the Secretary of Commerce, the 
   291                  Assistant to the President for National Security 
   292                  Affairs, and the Assistant to the President for 
   293                  Homeland Security, is hereby authorized to submit

    37                  Section 1. Background. On February 1, 2025, I

    41                  criminals at large, and illicit drugs constitutes an 
    42                  unusual and extraordinary threat, which has its source

    44                  national security, foreign policy, and economy of the

    46                  authority under section 1702(a)(1)(B) of IEEPA to

    51                  Executive Order of February 1, 2025, titled ``Imposing 
    52                  Duties to Address the Situation at Our Northern 
    53                  Border'' (``the Executive Order of February 1, 2025''), 
    54                  I have determined that the Government of Canada has 
    55                  taken immediate steps designed to alleviate the illegal 
    56                  migration and illicit drug crisis through cooperative 
    57                  actions. Further time is needed, however, to assess 
    58                  whether these steps constitute sufficient action to 
    59                  alleviate the crisis and resolve the unusual and 
    60                  extraordinary threat beyond our northern border.
    61  
    62                  Sec. 3. Pause. (a) In recognition of the steps taken by 
    63                  the Government of Canada, and in order to assess 
    64                  whether the threat described in section 1 of this order

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".

doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty
